title: Bayesian reasoning in plain English
summary: Estimate with words, update with evidence. Pick a phrase such as “likely” and see Sherman Kent's 1964 reference range beside every answer 46 people gave for it in an online survey, then choose the number you mean. Answer three plain questions (before, how likely the evidence if true, and if false) for an updated estimate on a 0–100% axis, rounded, with natural frequencies, an optional range from your phrase choices, and odds and likelihood ratio under Show calculation. Chain evidence in an editable reasoning trail, start from six offline examples or your own hypothesis, and save the trail as a narrated beamdswitch deck. Works offline, from file:// and in an iframe.
